why: options — the operator states in its own words that its signature item's wafer is gluten-free: 東山アイスもなか 「原材料に北陸産もち米のみを用いた最中種は自然な甘みと香ばしい風味が特徴のグルテンフリー」, and it publishes an アレルギー原材料 line for every gelato flavour, of which exactly one (金沢大野醤油＆焦がしキャラメル: 乳/卵/大豆/小麦) contains 小麦. 雪見アイスもなか is 最中種＋求肥＋粒餡 and the 2F menu is わらび餅・あんみつ・寒天・餡子 — all rice/agar/bean. Not 'high': どら焼き/チョコどら生地 and the deep-fried 金沢おでんカレーパン are made and handled in the same small shop, and no cross-contact protocol is published. But 'no' is wrong in the dangerous direction — it warns a celiac off a shop that labels its allergens and sells a rice-wafer signature.

why: ask — the record is internally inconsistent: it awards vegan_status 'ask' on the reasoning that 'a plant-based course might be arranged if requested well ahead', then awards gf_confidence 'no' on exactly the same facts. The page documents the mechanism for both — 「離れのお部屋は一名様から二〇名様まで承っております」 and 「人数、内容の変更は三日前の正午までにご連絡お願い致します」 — a made-to-order kaiseki in a detached private room that accepts content changes three days out. 'ask' is the correct tier for a place with no GF programme but a real advance-request channel; 'no' should be reserved for kitchens where the answer cannot change. Not higher than 'ask': no allergen information is published anywhere on the site, soy-sauce preparations (土佐煮, 柚庵焼き) are on the standard bento, and /news/ advertises お座敷天婦羅.
